title: Sequential weight snapshotting and KV primer with slot-based admission
creator: Aisha Khan
description:
Problem: Cold starts in Dedicated fleets remain a major factor in P95/P99 latency and unpredictable tail behavior for tenant traffic spikes. Existing warm strategies preload weights and occasionally seed KV, but they often load more than needed or race with admission bursts, wasting GPU memory and delaying useful priming.

Goal: Implement a slot-based admission controller combined with sequential weight snapshotting and a lightweight KV primer that together reduce cold-start P95 by >=40% for medium-length contexts (2k-8k) while keeping steady-state memory overhead under 6% per node. The solution should gracefully integrate with existing autoscaling and fleet controls, enable tenant-prioritized warm slots, and expose observability for priming efficiency and priming-induced progress.

Approach summary:
1) Sequential weight snapshotting: instead of loading full model weights concurrently, stream compact snapshots (layer groups) in a prioritized sequence that prioritizes early-token attention layers and KV-relevant projection matrices. Snapshots are checksumed and cached as immutable artifacts to avoid duplicated work across nodes.
2) Slot-based admission controller: maintain a small number of warm "slots" per GPU serving shard. Each slot reserves bounded memory and a priming plan (which snapshots and KV prefixes to load). Incoming requests are admitted to either warm slots (fast path) or cold queue (standard cold-boot path). Slots are leased to tenants based on priority signals and recent traffic heat.
3) Lightweight KV primer: for each slot, run a non-blocking background KV primer that injects commonly observed prefixes and warm-up minibatches (micro-batches of 8-16 tokens sampled from tenant traces). The primer records hit-rate and prefix utility metrics to adapt future priming ROI.
4) Admission scoring and eviction: slots are scored by recency, tenant SLAs, and observed priming utility. Low-score slots are reclaimed with a graceful taper (redirect next N requests to fallback variants while allowing KV eviction to complete).
5) Autoscaler integration: expose slot occupancy and priming pressure as autoscaler signals (slot-utilization, priming-io, priming-latency) so the fleet controller can scale capacity ahead of sustained pressure.
6) Observability and rollout: add slot-level dashboards, per-tenant priming ROI charts, and synthetic cold-start benchmarks to validate SLOs during rollout.

Out-of-scope for this ticket: permanent model sharding redesign, cross-region warm pooling, and on-prem packaging changes (those are follow-ups).
acceptance_criteria:
- End-to-end implementation of slot-based admission controller and sequential snapshot loader running behind feature flag.
- KV primer that can run per-slot, with metrics emitted for primer hit-rate and priming-duration.
- Telemetry: slot_allocations, slot_evictions, slot_score, priming_time_ms, priming_kv_hits, priming_bytes_loaded.
- Demonstrated cold-start P95 reduction >=40% on internal benchmark harness for 2k-8k contexts with comparable steady-state cost (memory overhead <=6%).
- Integration tests showing autoscaler reacts to slot-utilization signal within configured threshold.
- Design doc reviewed and approved by infra and runtime teams, and a rollout plan created with canary percentages and abort criteria.
implementation_plan: Draft design doc and priming algorithm (owner: Marco)

Implement slot admission API and per-shard slot allocator
Develop KV primer service as background coroutine with sampling-based prefix selection
Expose metrics and build dashboards in Console (slot-level views)
Run controlled canaries against a subset of Dedicated fleet, collect SLO/ROI metrics
Iterate on scoring heuristic and eviction tapering based on canary feedback
Gradual rollout with autoscaler signal enabled; monitor cost and latency closely

2026-01-28 Marco Delgado: Ran 10k synthetic requests through canary harness. Observed priming CPU contention at high slot counts; throttled primer coroutine to token budget per second.
2026-01-31 QA: Integration test added for slot eviction taper; confirmed no request failures during eviction when taper configured to 3 requests.
2026-02-02 Marco Delgado: Updated ticket with early canary results — P95 cold-start improvement 41% in 2k contexts, memory overhead measured at 4.9%. Moving to broader canary next week.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Priming IO could contend with serving IO during bursts -> Mitigation: priming runs at a token-rate budget and backs off on IO saturation signals.
Risk: Over-priming low-utility prefixes increases memory churn -> Mitigation: enforce priming utility threshold and TTL-based KV eviction policy.
Risk: Slot fragmentation leads to reduced throughput density -> Mitigation: use lease compaction routine during low-traffic windows to consolidate slots.
Risk: Interaction with autoscaler causes oscillation -> Mitigation: smooth slot-utilization signal with EWMA and add hysteresis on scale decisions.
testing_plan: Unit tests for snapshot loader, slot allocator, and KV primer. Integration test exercising admission path and eviction taper. Performance benchmark run daily during canary showing cold-start P50/P95/P99 and steady-state memory/throughput. Load tests to validate autoscaler reacts appropriately to slot-utilization signals.
